milestones.theme: A real system — the command language, file system, system services, and kernel executive stand on their own.
Installs and boots faithfully — the product installs to a target disk and reboots into a login.

The authenticity flip — RMS reads and writes genuine Files-11 ODS-2 over the executive ACP (the /vms passthrough retired on the runtime path), binary SYSUAF and Purdy login, and a userland that builds itself in-guest.

Cluster machinery — a real distributed lock manager over the SCS wire, RMS behind the DLM, and an executive-resident membership block (proven via the userspace SCS probe + single-node executive tests; a booted OVMX auto-joining a cluster is post-0.6, vms-110b).
Cluster wire fidelity — the SCS/MSCP connection manager answers a real VAX byte-for-byte.
Rejoin and satellite boot — a removed node rejoins under its own identity; diskless satellites boot from a served disk.
Feature-complete — a voting member joins, serves genuine ODS-2 storage, holds locks, and evacuates a live node; TCP/IP, DECnet, and the self-hosting toolchain reach done. The last features land here.

Hardened and proven — feature-frozen on 0.9: authenticity enforced by the executive, not by convention, and the whole system proven on real hardware and in extended cluster interop against a real VAX. The release you trust; fixes only.

workstreams.name: Executive substrate
workstreams.summary: Shared system state owned by the kernel executive: logical names, processes, locks, event flags, and devices survive across processes.

workstreams.name: Command-surface parity
workstreams.summary: Real breadth and depth across the DCL command set and system utilities — no facades.

workstreams.name: Self-hosting toolchain
workstreams.summary: OVMX builds OVMX from within: the librarian and linker run as native images with no host tools in the build path. The in-guest tcc is a labelled bootstrap; the faithful destination is the existing VMS GCC and MMK ports building on OVMX unchanged, over a genuine VMS-compatibility surface.

workstreams.name: Cluster configuration
workstreams.summary: Provision a node into a cluster the VMS way: SYSGEN parameters, AUTOGEN, CLUSTER_AUTHORIZE, and CLUSTER_CONFIG.

workstreams.name: TCP/IP networking
workstreams.summary: A VMS-faithful IP networking layered product — its own installable kit on the base operating system: the network device, sockets, configuration and management, the resolver, the client tools, and a bundled SSH.

workstreams.name: DECnet Phase IV
workstreams.summary: Clean-room DECnet: SET HOST and file transfer to and from a lab node.

workstreams.name: Kernel substrate
workstreams.summary: SYSKRNL: the OVMX executive layered over the Linux and NetBSD kernels — not a kernel of its own. Built from pinned upstream source with the VMS modules in-tree, curated per architecture.

workstreams.name: VAX as a first-class platform
workstreams.summary: OVMX runs natively on VAX through a NetBSD system kernel: the executive, ODS-2 storage, and DCL boot on real VAX emulation, co-released across every architecture.

releases.note: The cluster claim, made good: a booted OpenVMX node joins a real, running VMS Cluster and is counted as a member. On the lab's two-node VAXcluster, a fresh-booted OVMX node — with CAP_NET_RAW dropped, so the executive itself, not an ambient Linux capability, drove the Ethernet — brought up its cluster port, opened an SCS virtual circuit to a live VAX, connected the VMS$VAXcluster connection manager, and was admitted through the membership transition. The existing members' own accounting counted it: VAX1's F$GETSYI("CLUSTER_NODES") reported 3, sustained for the full ten-minute run; SHOW CLUSTER listed the node with STATUS=MEMBER; SDA showed a genuine, sequential Cluster System Block (CSID 00010003, following the VAXes' 00010001/00010002) with the member flag. The whole join runs inside the executive (vms.ko) — SCS, the connection manager, the PE/virtual-circuit transport, the DLM rebuild, and the state-transition barrier — not a userspace daemon. And it is crash-safe: both real VAXes stayed up the entire run with zero bugchecks, the release-gating invariant that OpenVMX must never emit a frame that can crash a peer. That safety is enforced two ways — a runtime emit-guard that drops any frame violating the measured crash-safe envelope, and a post-hoc wire-safety audit calibrated against 234k real cluster frames — after a hunt (E55–E85) that found and closed every crash-vector in the lab, never in production, the last being a transaction-close frame whose mandatory field VMS asserts nonzero. Honest scope: this edition JOINS an existing cluster (it does not boot satellites or form a cluster from nothing); quorum votes are computed and displayed but not yet enforced; and the member committed the transition without an on-wire barrier-release frame, a tracked follow-on. Configure it the VMS way: @SYS$MANAGER:CLUSTER_CONFIG_LAN.COM (docs/cluster-configuration.md).

Three more rungs up the self-hosting and networking long poles, no cluster-participation claim. DECnet Phase IV gains a real transport: an NSP logical-link connection service — establish (Connect Initiate/Confirm), carry data segments with acknowledgement and in-order sequencing, tear down (Disconnect Initiate/Confirm), and give up honestly (retransmit then abandon as unreachable) — proven on the wire between two nodes, byte-identical, the layer SET HOST and file transfer will ride. VMS condition handling gains its third authentic rung: the real Alpha invocation-context primitives (LIB$GET_INVO_*) walk the genuine procedure-descriptor and register-save-area chain, so an unwind can transfer into an ancestor frame that armed no explicit anchor — the mechanism a bare 'return to main' and compiler exception handling need — replacing the last piece of emulation on the software path. And the compiler runtime's file layer gains a real RMS veneer: a C-RTL stdio surface that routes fopen/fwrite/fread/fclose to genuine RMS create/put/get/close over the executive ACP, proven un-fakeably — a file written through the veneer is then seen on the real Files-11 ODS-2 volume by an independent reader, with a genuine File ID and version a POSIX bootstrap cannot forge; wiring it into the alpha port image is scoped as tracked follow-on work.

Four increments up the self-hosting and networking long poles. DECnet Phase IV gets its first real engine: a userspace daemon (DECNETD.EXE) opens an Ethernet datalink, emits and receives the routing HELLO on cadence, and drives a per-neighbour adjacency state machine — the raw socket hidden behind a VMS-authentic surface (an executor node, a circuit, SHOW ADJACENT NODES), the same way the cluster's SCS daemon hides its datalink; proven byte-exact against a real-VAX capture and live on the wire between two nodes. VMS condition handling gains its first authentic rung: SYS$SETEXV establishes real per-thread exception vectors and the dispatcher walks the genuine call-frame chain in the VMS four-stage search order with a real mechanism array, replacing a flat handler-stack emulation (the deeper frame-transfer unwind and hardware-exception unification are staged behind it). The compiler port's file workload is proven over genuine Files-11 ODS-2 through the executive ACP — versioning (a file created twice yields ;1 and ;2, which a POSIX overwrite cannot), wildcard directory enumeration with real File IDs, and fail-honest RMS$_FNF — though the port image's own C-RTL binding to that RMS engine (versus the bootstrap POSIX path) remains separate follow-on work. And a phantom is retired: the alpha cross-compiler's reported -O0 union-type-pun 'miscompile' was the VMS data model itself (long is 32-bit, matching DEC C), not a compiler defect — the test was corrected and a DEC C behavior-compatibility architecture drafted. No cluster-participation claim: the cluster machinery is real, but a booted OVMX auto-joining a cluster is not yet built.

A runtime-fidelity cleanup. $CREPRC no longer leaks debug text to the error stream: two unconditional diagnostic writes fired on stderr on every single process creation (visible in the boot and harness logs), which real VMS never does. They are removed — process creation is now silent on the error path — with no change to $CREPRC behavior, only its output.

An authenticity fix on the process-creation path. A RUN/UIC identity override requested by an unauthenticated creator is correctly refused with SS$_NOPRIV — but until now that refusal left a phantom process: $CREPRC named and registered the subprocess in the executive before deciding whether the /UIC override could be honored, so on refusal a live process control block persisted under the refused name and $GETJPI could find it. $CREPRC now takes the stamp-versus-refuse decision from its own arguments before it registers or names anything, so a refused override touches the executive not at all — no PCB, nothing to find. The authorized-override and plain-detached paths are unchanged and the LARP guard is not weakened; this closes the gap by construction, since a refused grandchild issues zero executive calls.

Executive robustness on the /NOWAIT subprocess path. LIB$SPAWN's asynchronous completion now fires even when a subprocess is killed WITHOUT calling $EXIT — a SIGKILL, a crash, a segfault — where before the parent would wait forever: the executive delivers an SS$_ABORT completion at reap time (setting the parent's event flag and queuing its AST) as it reclaims the dead child, at both reclaim points, so a /NOWAIT LIB$SPAWN is now safe against abnormal child termination. Also hardens the test surface: a cross-process publish-versus-translate race in the mailbox-by-logical-name harness is fixed deterministically (a real happens-before handshake, not a timeout), proven quiet across repeated runs.

Two more rungs, one on each of the networking and self-hosting long poles. DECnet Phase IV gains its router-hello codec — the L1/L2 router variant of the routing HELLO (spec-derived from the public DNA Phase IV routing spec and cross-checked against public tooling, its trailing router-list carried as opaque bytes rather than fabricated, and flagged to promote once a real router specimen is captured) — so the adjacency layer can now see routers, not just endnodes. And GCC self-hosting clears its pipeline rung: the executive drives a real multi-stage subprocess pipeline the VMS way — each stage spawned /NOWAIT via SYS$CREPRC, its completion signalled by the executive's event-flag/AST facility, its $STATUS read back by process id and checked before the next stage launches, inter-stage data flowing over an RMS scratch file — proven end to end on the QEMU kernel harness against a real /dev/vms (a four-stage chain runs in order; a mid-chain failure halts the pipeline). The GCC driver's process model now works on OVMX; only the real compiler-stage images remain to be dropped in behind it.
